hook: Tuza's triangle-cover bound holds for some sparse-enough graphs with at most four triangles per edge
summary: Tuza's conjecture says the fewest edges needed to hit every triangle is at most twice the most edge-disjoint triangles. The author proves it for graphs where each edge sits in at most four triangles, with limits on the densest edges and on average degree, using edge reductions, discharging and computer-checked certificates. A density condition is still required, and the general conjecture stays open.
title: Triangle-overlap cores and density bounds for Tuza's conjecture
